scope: ArtformScores only; nine dedicated handoffs and the Lean-related algebra-of-scores part of the ledger umbrella handoff. No physics experiments or literature audit.

judgements.title: Merging
judgements.reason: Both shear-merging identities over any commutative ring; the zero-step law is also covered in R2.

judgements.title: Whitehead's rule
judgements.reason: Unit-valued Whitehead matrix and both conjugations agree with the ledger, including stencil powers and signs.

judgements.title: Balanced movers
judgements.reason: The product of laws is correct, but the ledger time-order word realizes diag(u^-1, u).

judgements.title: Time reversal
judgements.reason: List reversal with negated stencils gives the inverse law for every score; list syntax retains all signed words.

judgements.title: Blocking
judgements.reason: Restriction of scalars through a finite basis equals the realizer of the explicitly placed blocked steps.

judgements.title: Red-black on the blocked artform
judgements.reason: The two kicks merge, the blocked shift exchanges the orders, and descendability implies the stated obstruction.

judgements.title: The coset basis of a sublattice
judgements.reason: The unique representative hypothesis is precisely the coset partition, with the correct subgroup-ring action.

judgements.title: Red-black on the checkerboard, with the face form
judgements.reason: The plane basis, x squared, face-stencil coefficients and nonzero obstruction are all asserted with 2 invertible.

judgements.title: One dimension, every dial
judgements.reason: Every determinant-one Laurent matrix over every field is a score, with no extra hypothesis on its entries.

judgements.title: One dimension, the dials Z/p^k
judgements.reason: All prime powers are covered, including k = 0; the nilpotent reduction kernel is proved rather than assumed.

judgements.title: One dimension, every dial Z/n
judgements.reason: All positive moduli are covered through prime powers and CRT; excluding ZMod 0 correctly excludes the integer ring.

judgements.title: The index
judgements.reason: The determinant obstruction excludes every diag(a,1) with a different from 1, including the running shift example.

judgements.title: One mode on a prime dial
judgements.reason: Surjectivity and equality iff equality in the presented group establish completeness for exactly the four specified primes.

judgements.title: The class of a law
judgements.reason: The left eigenvector and equality of ideal classes under GL processing use the actual quadratic quotient ring.

judgements.title: The trivial class
judgements.reason: Both directions of trivial ideal class iff a cyclic vector are stated; the cyclic basis intertwines with the companion.

judgements.title: One class, one law up to processing
judgements.reason: Nonzero law ideals and the full same-class iff GL conjugacy are asserted, without requiring invertible ideals.

judgements.title: Every class is a law's
judgements.reason: Over a PID every nonzero integral ideal occurs; denominator clearing represents all fractional ideal classes.

judgements.title: The reading
judgements.reason: Only output invariance is stated; the submitted reading claim also requires completeness and its closed form.

judgements.title: Palindromes
judgements.reason: Equal diagonal entries imply the exact reflection/inverse matrix identity, including characteristic 2.

judgements.title: The crystallographic pulls
judgements.reason: The orders 6, 4, 3 are exact, and pull 4 has infinite order; the other pulls are covered by T13:growth.

judgements.title: The caller's cut
judgements.reason: The cut formula is correct, but the submitted cancellation iff is absent and needs nondegenerate or universal quantification.

judgements.title: Every method is light
judgements.reason: The recurrence follows the actual painted permutations; pointwise walls and doubled bonds encode the interval decomposition.

judgements.title: Plain hunt is light in a mirror box
judgements.reason: The fold formula, motion at walls and exact row congruence for N at least 3 express the claimed light paths and course.

judgements.title: The modes of the mirror box
judgements.reason: Explicit cosine eigenvectors, independence, exhaustive eigenvalues and periodic oscillatory solutions are asserted.

judgements.title: The presentation of the bells
judgements.reason: The actual neighbour swaps are expressive and faithful for the A-type Coxeter presentation for every positive number of positions.

judgements.title: Rankin's parity
judgements.reason: The permutation condition, coset choice invariant, sign formula and sign of a Hamiltonian cycle match the source.

judgements.title: The lifting lemma
judgements.reason: The quotient permutation is both well-defined on every coset and an extent, under the stated normal subgroup hypothesis.

judgements.title: The Fibonacci rule
judgements.reason: Every odd prime is covered for SL and the center quotient PSL; fibRank is the least positive Fibonacci zero. A positive witness exists in ExtentTable.some7.

judgements.title: One back-step
judgements.reason: The translation is faithful, but its Non-vacuity section only excludes a one-back-step example; it supplies no positive witness.

judgements.title: Kicks with back-moves never ring
judgements.reason: The claimed matrix and both nonexistence results hold for every n at least 3, with composite PSL explicitly the quotient by signs.

judgements.title: The balance of back-steps
judgements.reason: The new cardinality identity counts actual exceptional steps and targets on every invariant union of cosets.

judgements.title: The two squares need two back-turns
judgements.reason: The concrete corner permutations define the group; exact orders and existence/minimality of two back-turns are proved.

judgements.title: The fewest back-steps
judgements.reason: The minima include existence; n = 8 is correctly left undecided at zero while excluding exactly one and two.

judgements.title: The table of forward extents
judgements.reason: The counts are of Hamiltonian-cycle permutations, not words with a chosen origin; all listed existence and nonexistence clauses are explicit.

judgements.title: Ringing on a lattice only transports
judgements.reason: Shift-equivariance forces a finite channel permutation with channelwise translations after a positive power, in any cell group.

judgements.title: The tick's orders and growth
judgements.reason: The full finite-order iff, both parabolic power formulas and hyperbolic trace growth match Theorem Q.

judgements.title: The step groups
judgements.reason: The actual generated subgroups, congruence conditions, equality criterion and finite/infinite indices match the table.

judgements.title: The free step groups
judgements.reason: Injectivity of the free-group lift expresses freeness on the specified generators, including every real pull at least 4.

judgements.title: The regular map of a dial
judgements.reason: Explicit determinant-defined incidences, directed-edge torsor, counts, degree, triangles and action preservation match the combinatorial map.

judgements.title: The tetrahedron, the octahedron and the icosahedron
judgements.reason: The numerical counts are proved; no identification with the three named incidence structures is stated.

judgements.title: The steps are turns
judgements.reason: The state action and determinant formulas give the exact edge test; the complete positive-modulus unit-square list includes the harmless zero-ring dial.

judgements.title: The cells that a tick fixes
judgements.reason: Trace obstructions and the explicit fixed sets give the tick criterion; the exploding-mode exclusions and four orders are included.

judgements.title: The two squares are the projective line over F₅
judgements.reason: The explicit labelling conjugates the turns into the projective action; generation, S5, uniqueness and square-determinant clauses are included.

judgements.title: Commutation
judgements.reason: The positive matrix commutator is correct; the ledger score commutator needs the opposite sign.

judgements.title: The fewest steps
judgements.reason: At most two steps is the correct treatment of identities and shears; the nonzero Strang coefficient forces at least three.

judgements.title: The index as a group
judgements.reason: The group statement is restricted to fields; the ledger also covers composite dials, whose units need not be monomials.

judgements.title: Face and link
judgements.reason: Intertwining and ideal inclusions do not establish the claimed normalization/gluing map; arbitrary scores need not be glued.

judgements.title: The criterion for palindromes
judgements.reason: Both directions use an invertible reversing matrix with square negative determinant, correcting the old missing square condition.

judgements.title: The caller's rule decides the cancellation
judgements.reason: The three Boolean shares and their exact mean cuts are proved; numerical convergence orders are outside this entry.

judgements.title: One cue
judgements.reason: The indicator/shift commutation iff is precise; it distinguishes uniform sets from noninvariant coin outcomes without claiming every random outcome fails.

judgements.title: The duet
judgements.reason: The uniform finite counts and Cartesian-source constancy theorem formalize the shared-cue claim; phrase legality remains in the textbook library.

judgements.title: The curve of the leapfrog phase
judgements.reason: The parametrization identities are proved; nodality, uniqueness of the singularity and the normalization claim are not stated.

judgements.title: The classes of the leapfrog phase
judgements.reason: The classification is onto and faithful for processing, with zero-mode, cyclic-vector, reversal and explicit representative values pinning the map.

judgements.title: The count of the classes
judgements.reason: The count is of the quotient of all laws of the phase, with the split/nonsplit sizes and the sharp gluing-subgroup bound.

judgements.title: The split node
judgements.reason: Evaluation at the chosen square root is the explicit group isomorphism and carries the gluing subgroup to the specified generators.

judgements.title: The schemes of the leapfrog phase
judgements.reason: All four concrete scores and both face/link forms have the asserted phase and processing representatives.

judgements.title: The magic step
judgements.reason: Every law has the triangular normal form; the complete invariant is pinned by both crossing values, with surjectivity and all three exceptional classes.

judgements.title: The count at the magic step
judgements.reason: The cardinality of all processing classes at the magic phase is (field size - 1)/2 + 3.

judgements.title: The schemes at the magic step
judgements.reason: Cyclic vectors, both zero-mode tests and the diagonal split movers place the concrete schemes in the claimed classes.

judgements.title: The palindromes of the leapfrog phase
judgements.reason: The complete palindrome-existence iff lists exactly the unglued, trivial and square-root/kappa alternatives, with actual processing.

judgements.title: A fixed class without a palindrome
judgements.reason: Each of the fourteen concrete laws has the right phase, is processed into its inverse, and is processed from no equal-diagonal law.

judgements.title: The presentations of the step groups
judgements.reason: The normal-closure iff uses exactly the table relators; the two congruence-group isomorphisms are also stated.

judgements.title: PSL(2, 5) is the alternating group
judgements.reason: The sign quotient of the actual SL(2,5) is isomorphic to the alternating group on five letters.
